scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 (Undergraduate Students) - Embassy Recommendation
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan

existing.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 (Undergraduate Students) funds international students who will study at Japanese national universities as undergraduates. MEXT publishes the terms in the FY2027 Application Guidelines and the application is made through a Japanese embassy or consulate general, or through a university recommendation. The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition at the accepting university and provides round-trip airfare. Under embassy recommendation the scholarship runs for five years including one year of Japanese language training.
eligibility: Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible
In principle born on or after 2 April 2002 (under 25 at application)
Completed 12 years of schooling, or a school equivalent to a Japanese upper secondary school, or passed an academic qualification examination equivalent to 12 years of schooling
Able to arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027
Willing to study in Japanese and to deepen understanding of Japan
In good physical and mental health, evidenced by a physician-signed certificate in the prescribed format
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country with diplomatic relations with Japan, be under 25 years of age, and have completed 12 years of school education or a course equivalent to a Japanese high school.
benefits: Full tuition exemption for the scholarship period
One year of Japanese language and other preparatory education (ABK College for humanities/social sciences, Osaka University for natural sciences)
Round-trip airfare between the home country and Japan
Settlement support and allowance described in the guidelines
coverage: Tuition exempted at the accepting national university
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided under embassy recommendation
requirements: Submit two application packets, one of originals and one of copies
Documents must be in Japanese or English, with a Japanese or English translation attached if written in another language
Write the document number from 1 to 9 in the upper right corner of the first page of each document
All written academic examination subjects are taken by every applicant
Do not send application documents directly to MEXT in Japan
documents: Application Form (FY2027 form)
Direct Placement Preference Form (only if applicable, submitted after passing first screening)
Field of Study sheet
Academic transcript(s) from upper secondary school and, if applicable, university
Certificate of graduation or certificate of prospective graduation
Recommendation letter from the president/dean or academic advisor
Medical certificate in the prescribed form signed by a physician
Abstracts of theses (if applicable)
Certificate of language proficiency, 2 copies (only if the applicant holds one)
Certificate of enrollment (only for applicants currently enrolled at a university)
Two complete application packets: one original set and one copy set
application_method: Embassy recommendation: submit the full packet to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's country of nationality by the deadline that mission sets
University recommendation: apply to a Japanese university that holds an MEXT recommendation quota; that university submits the recommendation to MEXT
existing.selection_notes: First screening is conducted by the Japanese diplomatic mission using document review, written academic examinations and an interview. Direct placement without preparatory education is available for applicants with sufficient Japanese ability, mainly in Social Sciences and Humanities.
existing.duration: 5 years including one year of Japanese language training at ABK College or Osaka University (7 years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary science and 6-year pharmacy); up to a standard school year under university recommendation
existing.application_period: Recruitment runs April-May of the year before arrival in Japan; embassy first screening May-August
existing.deadline_display: "Recruitment for those arriving in Japan next April is made between April and May of the previous year. First screening is conducted between May and August by the Japanese Embassies or Consulates General."
existing.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), Japan

existing.description: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2026 (Japanese Studies Students) funds international undergraduates who major in Japanese language or Japanese culture to study for one year at designated Japanese universities. Applicants must already have studied Japanese studies for at least one year and must remain enrolled at their home institution on return. MEXT states that it "offers scholarships to international students who wish to study for a period of one year at designated Japanese universities as Japanese Studies Students". The award pays a monthly scholarship, exempts tuition and provides round-trip airfare.
eligibility: Born between 2 April 1996 and 1 April 2008 (18 to 29 years old in principle)
Nationality of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan; Japanese nationals are not eligible
Undergraduate at a foreign (non-Japanese) university at the time of arriving in and leaving Japan, and still enrolled there on return
Majoring in a field related to the Japanese language and/or Japanese culture
Has studied Japanese studies at university for a total of one year or more as of 1 September 2026
Japanese language ability sufficient to receive education at a Japanese university in Japan
Physician-signed health certificate confirming no condition hindering study in Japan
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be between 18 and 29 years old, be enrolled as an undergraduate at a university outside Japan majoring in Japanese language or Japanese culture, and must have studied Japanese studies for a total of at least one year as of 1 September 2026.
benefits: Tuition exemption for the one-year course
One year of Japanese Studies Program study at a designated Japanese university
Round-trip airfare between the home country and Japan
coverage: Tuition exempted at the designated accepting university
Round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided under embassy recommendation
requirements: Submit the documents to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the applicant's country by the designated deadline
Select preferred universities only from the Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program and enter the course code
Documents must be in Japanese or English, with a Japanese or English translation attached otherwise
Write the document number from 1 to 8 in the upper right-hand corner of the first page of each document
Newly obtain a Student visa and enter Japan with resident status Student
documents: Application Form (FY2026 form)
Placement Preference Application Form (FY2026 form)
Certified academic transcript from the university the applicant currently attends, for all academic years up to the current year
Document verifying at least one year of Japanese language and culture study (only if not verifiable from the transcript)
Certificate of enrollment
Recommendation letter (free format; a sample is provided)
Medical certificate in the prescribed FY2026 form
Certificate of Japanese language ability (only if the applicant can supply proof)
Photograph taken within six months, 4.5 x 3.5 cm, attached to the Application Form
application_method: Embassy recommendation: submit the complete document set to the Japanese embassy or consulate general in the applicant's country of nationality
University recommendation: applicants may also reach the programme through a Japanese university recommendation
existing.selection_notes: The Japanese diplomatic missions conduct the first screening by examining the submitted documents, a written examination in Japanese, and an interview. MEXT then carries out the second screening and confirms the university placement.
existing.duration: One year of study at a designated Japanese university through the Japanese Studies Program course listed in the Course Guide of Japanese Studies Program
existing.application_period: Recruitment runs December of the previous year through February; embassy first screening January to February
existing.deadline_display: "Recruitment for those arriving in Japan next October is made between December of the previous year and the following February. The first screening is conducted between January and February by the Japanese embassies or consulates general."
existing.program_type: Government scholarship - national study abroad programme (embassy recommendation)
